guide.noAdb: Open Preferences (⚙), turn on advanced mode and choose where adb is.
noDevice: On the phone, open Settings › About phone and tap “Build number” 7 times to turn on Developer options.
In Settings › System › Developer options, turn on “USB debugging”.
Connect the phone to the computer with a USB data cable.
guide.noPermissions: On Linux the phone needs udev rules (package “android-sdk-platform-tools-common” or similar) and your user must be in the “plugdev” group. Then unplug and plug the cable again.
guide.unauthorized: Accept the “Allow USB debugging?” prompt on the phone. Tick “Always allow from this computer” so you don't have to repeat it.
guide.reauthorizeAfterAdbRoot: Turning on adb root mode restarts the connection, and the phone asks to authorize this computer again. Accept the prompt on the phone.
guide.connecting: If it takes long, unplug and plug the cable again.
guide.rootPending: A Magisk, KernelSU or similar prompt will appear on the phone. Tap “Grant”.
guide.noRoot: adbkeep needs administrator access to back up app data. There are two ways to get it:
guide.noRootSu: Root the phone with Magisk, KernelSU or similar.
guide.noRootAdb: On LineageOS and similar ROMs: Developer options › “Rooted debugging”.
guide.rootDenied: Open Magisk (or your root app) on the phone, allow access for “Shell” and press Retry.
guide.locked: Unlock the phone with your PIN, pattern or fingerprint. Until it has been unlocked once after starting, app data cannot be read.
guide.failed: Check the cable and press Retry.
